#====================================================================================================
# START - Testing Protocol - DO NOT EDIT OR REMOVE THIS SECTION
#====================================================================================================

# THIS SECTION CONTAINS CRITICAL TESTING INSTRUCTIONS FOR BOTH AGENTS
# BOTH MAIN_AGENT AND TESTING_AGENT MUST PRESERVE THIS ENTIRE BLOCK

# Communication Protocol:
# If the `testing_agent` is available, main agent should delegate all testing tasks to it.
#
# You have access to a file called `test_result.md`. This file contains the complete testing state
# and history, and is the primary means of communication between main and the testing agent.
#
# Main and testing agents must follow this exact format to maintain testing data. 
# The testing data must be entered in yaml format Below is the data structure:
# 
## user_problem_statement: {problem_statement}
## backend:
##   - task: "Task name"
##     implemented: true
##     working: true  # or false or "NA"
##     file: "file_path.py"
##     stuck_count: 0
##     priority: "high"  # or "medium" or "low"
##     needs_retesting: false
##     status_history:
##         -working: true  # or false or "NA"
##         -agent: "main"  # or "testing" or "user"
##         -comment: "Detailed comment about status"
##
## frontend:
##   - task: "Task name"
##     implemented: true
##     working: true  # or false or "NA"
##     file: "file_path.js"
##     stuck_count: 0
##     priority: "high"  # or "medium" or "low"
##     needs_retesting: false
##     status_history:
##         -working: true  # or false or "NA"
##         -agent: "main"  # or "testing" or "user"
##         -comment: "Detailed comment about status"
##
## metadata:
##   created_by: "main_agent"
##   version: "1.0"
##   test_sequence: 0
##   run_ui: false
##
## test_plan:
##   current_focus:
##     - "Task name 1"
##     - "Task name 2"
##   stuck_tasks:
##     - "Task name with persistent issues"
##   test_all: false
##   test_priority: "high_first"  # or "sequential" or "stuck_first"
##
## agent_communication:
##     -agent: "main"  # or "testing" or "user"
##     -message: "Communication message between agents"

# Protocol Guidelines for Main agent
#
# 1. Update Test Result File Before Testing:
#    - Main agent must always update the `test_result.md` file before calling the testing agent
#    - Add implementation details to the status_history
#    - Set `needs_retesting` to true for tasks that need testing
#    - Update the `test_plan` section to guide testing priorities
#    - Add a message to `agent_communication` explaining what you've done
#
# 2. Incorporate User Feedback:
#    - When a user provides feedback that something is or isn't working, add this information to the relevant task's status_history
#    - Update the working status based on user feedback
#    - If a user reports an issue with a task that was marked as working, increment the stuck_count
#    - Whenever user reports issue in the app, if we have testing agent and task_result.md file so find the appropriate task for that and append in status_history of that task to contain the user concern and problem as well 
#
# 3. Track Stuck Tasks:
#    - Monitor which tasks have high stuck_count values or where you are fixing same issue again and again, analyze that when you read task_result.md
#    - For persistent issues, use websearch tool to find solutions
#    - Pay special attention to tasks in the stuck_tasks list
#    - When you fix an issue with a stuck task, don't reset the stuck_count until the testing agent confirms it's working
#
# 4. Provide Context to Testing Agent:
#    - When calling the testing agent, provide clear instructions about:
#      - Which tasks need testing (reference the test_plan)
#      - Any authentication details or configuration needed
#      - Specific test scenarios to focus on
#      - Any known issues or edge cases to verify
#
# 5. Call the testing agent with specific instructions referring to test_result.md
#
# IMPORTANT: Main agent must ALWAYS update test_result.md BEFORE calling the testing agent, as it relies on this file to understand what to test next.

#====================================================================================================
# END - Testing Protocol - DO NOT EDIT OR REMOVE THIS SECTION
#====================================================================================================

##         -comment: "USER-REPORTED BUG: 'Scan replies' on candidate Abishek Sekar (sekarabishek@gmail.com) returned 'no replies in your inbox' even though the connected Gmail (kangabhijeet@gmail.com) had a reply from that candidate containing notice period and compensation details. Root cause: admin@ats.com's existing google_tokens were issued BEFORE we added gmail.readonly to SCOPES — verified via GET /api/calendar/status returning can_read_inbox=false and scopes=[calendar, gmail.send, userinfo.email, openid]. Gmail's messages().list() call rejected the request with a 403/insufficient-scope error, which gmail_reader.search_replies_from() was catching and returning an empty list — so the endpoint reported 'replies: 0' as if there were no matching messages. Fix: (1) search_replies_from() now returns a `(messages, error)` tuple; on any exception we classify the underlying error into a short reason string via _classify_gmail_error (insufficient_scope / invalid_token / rate_limited / network_error / gmail_api_error) instead of swallowing it. (2) POST /api/candidates/{id}/scan-replies pre-checks the granted scopes on the fresh user document — if `gmail.readonly` isn't in tokens.scope, it returns `{ok:false, reason:'missing_readonly_scope', message:'Reconnect your Gmail from My Integrations to grant inbox-read permission.'}` WITHOUT calling Gmail. (3) If the API call itself errors, the response now carries the classified reason so the frontend can nudge the user to reconnect. (4) Also added `in:anywhere` to the Gmail query so replies filed under Spam/Trash are included in the scan. (5) reply_scanner (background loop) updated for the new tuple return type; logs gmail_error at INFO instead of returning empty silently. (6) Frontend CandidateProfilePage.scanReplies handler now shows a distinct toast for `missing_readonly_scope|insufficient_scope|invalid_token` with a Reconnect action button that navigates to /my-integrations. Live-verified via curl on admin@ats.com (who has the old token): POST /api/candidates/{id}/scan-replies returned `{ok:false, reason:'missing_readonly_scope', message:'Reconnect your Gmail from My Integrations to grant inbox-read permission.', replies:0, updated:false}` — exactly the actionable error the user needed. Needs backend testing to verify: (1) POST /api/candidates/{id}/scan-replies as admin@ats.com — returns 200 with reason='missing_readonly_scope' and the specific message string (not silent 'replies:0'). (2) POST scan-replies for a candidate without email — reason='no_email_on_candidate'. (3) POST scan-replies for a candidate with email while the user has no google_tokens — reason='no_gmail_connected'. (4) Regression: reply_scanner background loop tolerates the same missing-scope condition and does not crash — verify by tailing /var/log/supervisor/backend.err.log for 45+ seconds after backend restart and looking for the scheduler tick without exceptions. (5) The response shape for scan-replies includes new key `message` (string, human-readable) alongside `reason` when ok=false. (6) Also confirm: users who DO have gmail.readonly granted still get {ok:true, replies:N, ...}. If no test user with readonly scope exists in the environment, skip this positive-path check and note it. IMPORTANT for testing agent: the test candidate 'Abishek Sekar' with email sekarabishek@gmail.com does NOT exist in this test DB — do NOT try to create real Gmail interactions. Just verify the error path is now visible via the API response."


## backend:
##   - task: "Bug fix: feedback reminder emails were being sent multiple times per pass (spam) — enforce send-once idempotency"
##     implemented: true
##     working: "NA"
##     file: "backend/reminder_scheduler.py, backend/feedback_emails.py, backend/routes_interviews.py, backend/email_templates.py, backend/routes_career.py"
##     stuck_count: 0
##     priority: "high"
##     needs_retesting: true
##     status_history:
##         -working: "NA"
##         -agent: "main"
##         -comment: "USER-REPORTED BUG: feedback reminder emails were arriving 4 times every ~30 min. Root cause: REMINDER_INTERVALS_HOURS=[2,8,12,24] and the scheduler looped ALL thresholds in a single pass — for an interview completed ≥24h ago with no prior reminders, one pass sent 4 emails (one per threshold). Additional risk: no atomic claim before send meant overlapping passes could double-send. Fix implemented: (1) Changed REMINDER_INTERVALS_HOURS to [12, 24] (user's spec: only 12h and 24h). (2) Rewrote reminder_scheduler.py: for each interview × interviewer we now pick only the SINGLE highest applicable threshold that hasn't been claimed yet — never spamming multiple thresholds in a single pass. (3) Before each send, we atomically claim the (interview, interviewer, threshold) tuple via a conditional Mongo update with $addToSet; if the update matches 0 documents (concurrent pass beat us), we skip that interviewer. If the actual gmail send subsequently fails, we roll back the claim with $pull so the next pass retries. (4) Made POST /api/interviews/{id}/complete idempotent — the state transition uses a conditional update `{status: {$ne: 'feedback_pending'}}` so a retried call matches 0 docs and returns the current state WITHOUT re-firing notifications or the initial scorecard-request email. (5) Added `scorecard_email_sent_to` array on interview documents; send_scorecard_request skips any interviewer already listed (protects against manual re-calls of complete). (6) Added opt-in `dedup_window_seconds` parameter to send_template() in email_templates.py which consults email_log for prior successful sends of the same (template_key, to_email) within N seconds; used by the career-portal application_received auto-reply with a 24h window so a candidate accidentally submitting the apply form twice does NOT get two confirmation emails. Live-tested: restart is clean; no lint errors. Needs backend testing to verify: (1) POST /api/interviews/{id}/complete called twice in a row — second call must not re-send the initial scorecard-request email (check email_log count for that recipient/template between the two calls). (2) Interview with completed_at set to 25h ago and empty reminders_sent — one scheduler pass must send AT MOST ONE reminder per interviewer (the 24h one, not both 12h and 24h). (3) Interview with completed_at at 13h ago — one pass sends 12h reminder; a manual re-invocation of the scheduler pass 5 min later must NOT re-send. (4) POST /api/career/public/apply twice for the same candidate email within 24h — first call sends application_received, second call returns {sent:false, reason:'duplicate_recent_send'} and no additional email_log 'sent' row exists. (5) REMINDER_INTERVALS_HOURS constant equals [12, 24]. (6) Regression: normal /complete flow still fires the initial scorecard email once. (7) Regression: manual /api/career/emails/send is unaffected — user-triggered emails still send even if a similar template was sent recently (no dedup applied there)."

##         -comment: "Three-part feature (July 2025): (1) Auto-parse candidate reply emails. New backend/gmail_reader.py fetches messages from a specific candidate's email via Gmail API (using the sender_user_id's OAuth creds; extracts plain-text or strips HTML to text). New backend/reply_parser.py sends the reply body to gpt-5.4-mini via emergentintegrations (system prompt forbids guessing; returns null for unmentioned fields) and extracts notice_period + expected_compensation. New backend/reply_scanner.py runs every 5 min (REPLY_SCAN_INTERVAL_SEC): iterates email_log rows with status='sent' from the last 30 days, skips candidates who already have both fields populated, calls gmail_reader.search_replies_from(after=email_log.created_at OR last_reply_scanned_at), parses each new reply via LLM, writes only fields the candidate lacks (never overwrites existing data), and logs activity/audit rows with actor=sender_user. Also added POST /api/candidates/{id}/scan-replies (admin+/recruiter, but requires user to be admin_or_higher) for manual on-demand triggering — uses the LOGGED-IN user's own Gmail creds. Added `gmail.readonly` to SCOPES in google_calendar.py; get_credentials_for_user() now uses the ACTUAL granted scopes (from tokens['scope']) when refreshing so existing users' tokens don't fail with invalid_scope — they must reconnect via /oauth/google/login to grant the new read scope. Added `expected_compensation` field to CandidateCreate + CandidateUpdate models in routes_candidates.py; also included in CANDIDATE_SENSITIVE_FIELDS in permissions.py so interview_panel & vendor users don't see it. (2) Per-user Gmail sending. Refactored _pick_sender_creds() in email_templates.py — now takes sender_user_id (renamed from recruiter_id) and, by default, ONLY uses that user's Gmail creds (no fallback). Added opt-in `allow_admin_fallback=True` used ONLY by routes_career.py's career-portal application_received auto-reply (system-triggered, no logged-in user). send_template() and send_custom() now accept sender_user_id explicitly; backwards-compat with recruiter_id kwarg preserved. POST /api/career/emails/send now (a) requires admin (super_admin/admin) role — recruiter/interview_panel/vendor get 403; (b) always passes sender_user_id=user['id'] so the email goes out from the LOGGED-IN admin's Gmail account, not a shared account. /api/calendar/status now also returns {scopes, can_read_inbox, can_send_email} so the frontend can nudge the user to reconnect if the read-inbox scope is missing. Live-tested: PUT /api/candidates/{id} with expected_compensation='22 LPA' saves & retrieves correctly; POST scan-replies returns {ok:true, replies:0, ...} without 500; POST /api/career/emails/send with admin@ats.com successfully sent an email (status 200, sent=1, gmail_id populated) — confirming per-user creds path works end-to-end. Needs backend testing: (1) POST /api/career/emails/send as super_admin — 200 (regression). (2) POST /api/career/emails/send as recruiter (create a recruiter test user if needed) — expect 403. (3) POST /api/career/emails/send as admin who has NOT connected Gmail — expect results[].reason='no_gmail_connected' with sent=false, no 500. (4) POST /api/candidates/{id} with expected_compensation='22 LPA' — 200; GET candidate returns it for admin, GET as interview_panel strips it. (5) POST /api/candidates/{id}/scan-replies as admin with no Gmail — {ok:false, reason:'no_gmail_connected'}. (6) POST /api/candidates/{id}/scan-replies for a candidate with no email — {ok:false, reason:'no_email_on_candidate'}. (7) Regression: GET /api/calendar/status returns new fields (scopes, can_read_inbox, can_send_email) without breaking existing keys. (8) Regression: career-portal POST /api/career/public/apply still triggers the auto-reply email (allow_admin_fallback=True path). (9) Reply scanner loop runs without exceptions on empty state (check backend logs for 'reply_scan_loop scheduled')."

FEATURE 1 (expected_compensation + sensitive-field stripping): ✅ Test 1.1: POST /api/candidates with expected_compensation='30 LPA' + notice_period='45 days' returns 200 with both fields echoed correctly. ✅ Test 1.2: GET /api/candidates/{id} as super_admin returns both expected_compensation and notice_period fields intact. ✅ Test 1.3: PUT /api/candidates/{id} with expected_compensation='32 LPA' updates successfully, GET returns updated value. ✅ Test 1.4: Created interview_panel test user, added to job team with salary_visible=false, logged in as panel user, GET /api/candidates/{id} correctly strips ALL sensitive fields (expected_compensation, notice_period, current_ctc, expected_salary all absent from response). ✅ Test 1.5: GET /api/candidates list as interview_panel user - none of the items contain expected_compensation or other sensitive fields. FEATURE 3 (per-user Gmail sending on POST /api/career/emails/send): ✅ Test 3.1: POST /api/career/emails/send as super_admin with candidate_ids:[valid_id] and template_key:'application_shortlisted' returns 200 with per-candidate results, sent=true and gmail_id populated (admin@ats.com has connected Gmail). ✅ Test 3.2: POST /api/career/emails/send as admin role (created test user with role='admin') returns 200 - endpoint correctly allows 'admin' role per require_roles('admin') at line 254 of routes_career_security.py. MISC REGRESSION TESTS: ✅ POST /api/auth/login works (200). ✅ GET /api/candidates works (200). ✅ GET /api/jobs works (200). ✅ GET /api/dashboard/stats works (200). ✅ Backend logs (/var/log/supervisor/backend.err.log) show 'reply_scan_loop scheduled — scanning candidate email replies every 5 minutes' on startup, no crash in scanner loop. All test candidates and test users cleaned up successfully. Implementation is production-ready with full RBAC enforcement and backwards compatibility maintained."

##         -comment: "Implemented Phase 1 of the permissions revamp. NEW ROLES: super_admin, admin, interview_panel, vendor (labels: 'Super Admin', 'Admin', 'Interview Panel', 'Agency / Vendor'). Legacy role names ('recruiter', 'interviewer') still work as aliases — recruiter→admin, interviewer→interview_panel. MIGRATION (idempotent, runs on startup via migrate_rbac.migrate_to_new_rbac): seeded admin emails admin@ats.com and kangabhijeet@gmail.com promoted to super_admin; recruiter role renamed to admin; interviewer role renamed to interview_panel; every existing job doc backfilled with team_members: []. Verified in DB: admin@ats.com/kangabhijeet@gmail.com are now super_admin, abhi.kang@context66.com is now admin, all 6 jobs have team_members array. NEW HELPERS in backend/permissions.py: role_satisfies(user_role, required_names) with ROLE_ALIASES so require_roles('admin') still passes super_admin; is_super_admin, is_admin_or_higher, is_interview_panel, is_vendor, can_manage_role, strip_job_sensitive, strip_candidate_sensitive, visible_job_ids_for_user. UPDATED auth.require_roles to use role_satisfies (backwards-compat for every existing route without touching them). ROLE HIERARCHY in routes_admin.py: only super_admin can create/delete/update-role-of super_admin users; admin can manage admin/interview_panel/vendor; can_manage_role() enforces this in POST /users, PUT /users/{id}, DELETE /users/{id}. NEW JOB TEAM MODEL: job.team_members = [{user_id, role_on_job: 'interview_panel'|'vendor', salary_visible: bool, added_by, added_by_name, added_at}]. NEW ENDPOINTS (admin+ only): GET /api/jobs/{id}/team → {job_id, members: [...enriched with user_name/user_email/user_role]}; POST /api/jobs/{id}/team {user_id, role_on_job, salary_visible} → adds member (rejects if user is already admin+ globally, or already on team); PATCH /api/jobs/{id}/team/{user_id} → toggle salary_visible or change role_on_job; DELETE /api/jobs/{id}/team/{user_id}. VISIBILITY RULES: (a) GET /api/jobs — admin+ sees all; interview_panel/vendor sees only jobs where they're in team_members. (b) GET /api/jobs/{id} — 403 if non-admin caller isn't on that job's team. (c) GET /api/candidates list — admin+ sees all; interview_panel sees candidates on their team's jobs; vendor sees only candidates where submitted_by == their user id AND on their team's jobs; legacy interviewer keeps old assigned-interviews scope. (d) GET /api/candidates/{id} — 403 if non-admin doesn't have visibility. FIELD STRIPPING: interview_panel and vendor get salary_range/budget/compensation/salary_min/salary_max stripped from job responses UNLESS their team_members entry has salary_visible=true; interview_panel additionally gets expected_salary/current_ctc/notice_period stripped from candidate responses. NEW /candidates/{id}/change-log and /jobs/{id}/change-log endpoints (admin+ only) — reads audit_log collection filtered by entity_type + entity_id, returns most-recent first. EXPANDED AUDIT: update_candidate and update_job now write field-level diffs (e.g. 'title: Old → New; status: open → paused') to audit_log so the change log surfaces every edit. VENDOR CAN CREATE CANDIDATES: POST /api/candidates now accepts 'vendor' role; vendor's candidates automatically get submitted_by = user.id, submitted_by_name, and source='vendor'; vendor must specify job_id and be on the team for that job (403 otherwise). BUG FIX: bulk_action delete guard was checking user['role'] != 'admin' which broke for super_admin — now uses is_admin_or_higher(). SEED updated for future fresh installs to use new role names. Verified end-to-end with a live test: created an interview_panel user, added them to 1 job, logged in as them — they see only that 1 job with salary_range/budget stripped; hitting the change-log endpoint as them returns 403 as expected. Needs testing agent to cover: (1) idempotent migration re-runs, (2) role hierarchy enforcement on user CRUD, (3) team CRUD endpoints (add/list/patch/remove), (4) candidate visibility for interview_panel + vendor + admin, (5) field stripping (salary_visible true vs false), (6) change-log endpoints (admin ok, non-admin 403), (7) audit diff format on candidate/job update, (8) vendor add-candidate flow (must be on team + own only)."

TEAM ENDPOINTS: ✅ POST /api/jobs/{id}/team adds members with enriched fields (user_name, user_email, user_role), ✅ duplicate add returns 409, ✅ adding admin/super_admin to team returns 422 (global access message), ✅ nonexistent user returns 404, ✅ invalid role_on_job returns 422, ✅ GET /api/jobs/{id}/team returns enriched member list, ✅ PATCH salary_visible works correctly, ✅ PATCH nonexistent member returns 404. INTERVIEW_PANEL VISIBILITY: ✅ GET /api/jobs returns exactly 1 job (only team jobs), ✅ salary fields correctly shown when salary_visible=true, ✅ salary fields correctly hidden when salary_visible=false, ✅ GET /api/jobs/{other_job} returns 403 (not on team), ✅ GET /api/candidates returns only candidates from team jobs, ✅ sensitive fields (expected_salary, current_ctc, notice_period) correctly stripped from all candidate responses, ✅ change-log endpoints return 403 for interview_panel. VENDOR VISIBILITY: ✅ GET /api/jobs returns exactly 1 job (only team jobs), ✅ salary fields correctly hidden, ✅ GET /api/candidates returns only vendor's own submitted candidates (0 initially), ✅ POST candidate to non-team job returns 403, ✅ POST candidate to team job succeeds with submitted_by=vendor_id and source='vendor', ✅ GET /api/candidates after POST includes new candidate, ✅ GET specific vendor candidate succeeds, ✅ super_admin sees ALL candidates including vendor-submitted (140 total). ## backend:
##   - task: "Send email(s) to one or many candidates via POST /api/career/emails/send (template or free-form)"
##     implemented: true
##     working: "NA"
##     file: "backend/routes_career_security.py, backend/email_templates.py"
##     stuck_count: 0
##     priority: "high"
##     needs_retesting: true
##     status_history:
##         -working: "NA"
##         -agent: "main"
##         -comment: "New endpoint POST /api/career/emails/send (admin/recruiter). Body: {candidate_ids:[...] (1..500), template_key?:string, subject?:string, html_body?:string}. Rules: if template_key is provided the template is looked up and used (subject/html_body, if also supplied, override the template's own subject/body per-send); if no template_key, both subject AND html_body are required. Variables ({{candidate_name}}, {{job_title}}, {{company_name}}, {{stage}}, {{candidate_first_name}}, {{candidate_email}}, {{primary_color}}) are rendered per-recipient using build_context_from_candidate. Sender Gmail creds are picked via existing _pick_sender_creds() (recruiter first, else first admin with connected Gmail). Also added a new helper email_templates.send_custom() that mirrors send_template() for free-form / overridden sends and logs to db.email_log with template_key='custom' or the specific template key. Response shape: {total, sent, failed, skipped_no_email, skipped_missing, results:[{candidate_id, name, email, sent, reason?, error?, gmail_id?, sender?}]}. Side effects: on each successful send, an audit_log 'career.email.sent' entry is added and an activities row (action='email_sent') is inserted so the send appears in the candidate timeline. Guardrails: candidate_ids must be a non-empty list up to 500; template_key returns 404 if unknown; no subject/body + no template returns 422; candidates missing from DB are counted in skipped_missing; candidates without an email are counted in skipped_no_email (not attempted). Needs backend testing: (1) POST /api/career/emails/send with 1 candidate + template_key='application_shortlisted' — response should have total=1, and either sent=1 (if a Gmail is connected in this env) OR sent=0 with results[0].reason='no_gmail_connected' (expected in most test envs). No 500. (2) POST with candidate_ids of 3 candidates + custom subject/html_body — response total=3, results has 3 entries all with proper reason/sent flags; each successful send should insert an activities row for that candidate_id (verify via GET /api/candidates/{id}/timeline). (3) POST with a candidate_id that has NO email — that entry's reason='no_email_on_candidate', sent=false, and skipped_no_email counter increments. (4) POST with a non-existent candidate_id in the list — that entry's reason='candidate_not_found' and skipped_missing counter increments; other real candidates still processed. (5) POST with template_key='does_not_exist' — 404. (6) POST with neither template_key nor subject/html_body — 422. (7) POST with empty candidate_ids [] — 422. (8) POST with 501 candidate_ids — 422. (9) Recruiter role can call the endpoint (not admin-only), interviewer/candidate get 403 via require_roles."

##   - task: "Auto-compress uploaded resumes (PDF/DOCX) to reduce storage footprint, without quality loss"
##     implemented: true
##     working: true
##     file: "backend/resume_compressor.py, backend/routes_resumes.py, backend/requirements.txt"
##     stuck_count: 0
##     priority: "high"
##     needs_retesting: false
##     status_history:
##         -working: "NA"
##         -agent: "main"
##         -comment: "Context: user is planning to scale to ~50,000 candidates and was worried about MongoDB storage (resumes are stored as base64 blobs embedded in Mongo documents, currently a 9.8GB dedicated volume). Investigated actual storage breakdown: candidate/note/activity metadata is tiny (~2KB/candidate), but resume files average ~312KB physical (base64 + WiredTiger overhead) each — at 50k candidates-with-resumes this could need ~15.6GB, exceeding the 9.8GB volume. User asked specifically for resumes to be auto-compressed to their lowest size WITHOUT sacrificing visibility/quality (as an alternative/complement to migrating storage off Mongo, which was proposed but not yet approved). Implemented new backend/resume_compressor.py: for PDFs, uses PyMuPDF (pymupdf==1.28.0, added to requirements.txt) to do lossless font-subsetting + garbage-collection + stream deflation (doc.subset_fonts() + doc.tobytes(garbage=4, deflate=True, deflate_images=True, deflate_fonts=True, clean=True)) — this never alters rendered visual/text content, purely removes redundant objects and re-encodes more efficiently. For DOCX (a ZIP archive), re-zips every internal part at max DEFLATE level (compresslevel=9) — content is byte-identical once unzipped. Always falls back to original bytes on any error or if the 'compressed' result isn't actually smaller (safe by construction). Wired into routes_resumes.py's _store_file() (used by both /resumes/parse and /resumes/parse/bulk), running via asyncio.to_thread so it doesn't block the event loop; crucially, text extraction for AI parsing (extract_text_from_bytes) still runs on the ORIGINAL uncompressed bytes BEFORE storage, so compression cannot affect parsing accuracy. Verified compression correctness by round-tripping fixture files through text-extraction after compression (byte-identical text recovered). Also ran a one-off retroactive migration (backend/migrate_compress_files.py) on all 14 existing real resume files already in the database: 2,084,531 -> 1,715,702 bytes (17.7% average reduction; real-world resumes like the Naukri/DEEPRAJ_PATHAK PDFs shrank 16-27%), then ran `db.runCommand({compact:'files'})` to reclaim ~1.8MB of physical storage immediately. Verified all 14 files still open correctly and yield non-empty extracted text post-compression (0 failures). NOT YET VERIFIED BY TESTING AGENT - needs backend testing: upload a new resume via POST /api/resumes/parse (single) using /app/tests/fixtures/resume_sarah_chen.pdf and resume_priya_patel.docx, confirm 200 response with correctly parsed fields (unaffected by compression), confirm the stored file (GET /api/files/{file_id}) downloads successfully and is a valid, openable PDF/DOCX (not corrupted) and is same-size-or-smaller than the original upload. Also test /api/resumes/parse/bulk with multiple files for the same. Also spot check a candidate's resume preview (PDF iframe + DOCX docx-preview renderer, both built in earlier session) still displays correctly for a freshly uploaded (now auto-compressed) file — full round trip: upload -> parse -> save candidate -> view profile -> preview renders -> download works."
##         -working: true
##         -agent: "testing"
##         -comment: "COMPREHENSIVE TESTING COMPLETED - ALL TESTS PASSED (100% pass rate for compression feature). Resume auto-compression feature tested thoroughly with all 5 test cases from review request: (1) ✅ PDF compression (resume_sarah_chen.pdf): Original 2059 bytes → Compressed 1688 bytes (18.0% reduction). Parsing successful (Sarah Chen, sarah.chen@example.com extracted correctly). Downloaded file is valid PDF (verified PDF header). (2) ✅ DOCX compression (resume_priya_patel.docx): Original 37009 bytes → Compressed 34666 bytes (6.3% reduction). Parsing successful (Priya Patel, priya.patel@example.org extracted correctly). Downloaded file is valid DOCX (verified ZIP header). (3) ✅ Bulk upload compression: POST /api/resumes/parse-bulk with resume_sarah_chen.pdf and resume_miguel_torres.pdf both returned status='success', valid file_ids, and correctly parsed data (Sarah Chen and Miguel Torres). (4) ✅ File retrieval: GET /api/files/{file_id} returns valid, openable files that are same size or smaller than originals. (5) ✅ Sanity checks: GET /api/jobs (200), GET /api/candidates?limit=5 (200), GET /api/dashboard/stats (200) - no regressions from backend changes. CRITICAL VERIFICATION: Text extraction for AI parsing happens on ORIGINAL bytes BEFORE compression, so parsing accuracy is completely unaffected by compression (verified by successful name/email extraction in all tests). Compression is lossless for visual content - PDFs use font-subsetting + garbage collection + stream deflation (no pixel changes), DOCX uses max-level re-zip (byte-identical content when unzipped). Implementation is production-ready and meets user's requirement to reduce storage footprint without sacrificing quality. Overall test suite: 60/61 tests passed (98.4% pass rate). The 1 failure is unrelated (interviewer login - user doesn't exist in DB, not a compression issue)."
##         -working: true
##         -agent: "main"
##         -comment: "ENHANCEMENT (Feb 2026 fork session): DOCX compression previously only re-zipped the archive at max DEFLATE level, missing the biggest real-world win — embedded images (profile photos/logos in word/media/*). Added _compress_docx_image() using Pillow: caps embedded images to max 1600px dimension and re-encodes (JPEG quality=85 optimized, or optimized PNG for non-photo formats), wrapped per-image in try/except inside the zip loop so one bad image can't break the whole file, falls back to original bytes if not smaller. Verified directly by main agent (self-tested, testing_agent unavailable/timed out this round): (1) unit test with a synthetic 3000x3000 PNG embedded in a docx — correctly downsized to 1600x1600, zip stayed valid (testzip() clean). (2) Re-ran existing resume_priya_patel.docx fixture through the full compress_resume() pipeline — still valid DOCX, extract_text_from_bytes() output byte-identical before/after compression (proves parsing accuracy unaffected). (3) Live UI screenshot verification on a real seeded candidate (Umesh Chauhan, DOCX resume with an embedded profile photo) — resume preview renders the photo and all text correctly post-compression, confirming no visual corruption. Low risk given the safe-fallback-on-any-error design plus direct verification above; recommend a light regression pass next time testing_agent is invoked for something else in this area."

##         -comment: "User imports ~100 candidates via CSV/Excel (no resume attached), then separately uploads CVs and wants the system to detect the resume belongs to an already-existing candidate (matched by name) and update/merge that candidate's info instead of creating a duplicate. Confirmed hybrid approach with user: email match = high-confidence (defaults to merge), name-only match = lower-confidence (defaults to create-new, user must opt in), no match = create new as before. BACKEND: added _find_match(parsed) helper in routes_resumes.py — case-insensitive exact match on email first, else case-insensitive exact match on name, returns {candidate_id, candidate_name, match_type} or None; wired into _parse_one so both POST /api/resumes/parse and /api/resumes/parse-bulk now return a 'match' field in each result alongside 'parsed'. Added new POST /api/candidates/{candidate_id}/merge-resume (admin/recruiter) in routes_candidates.py taking {file_id, parsed} — sets resume_file_id to the new file, and for each of name/email/phone/current_title/current_company/location/notice_period/skills/experience/education, only overwrites the existing candidate's field if the resume provided a non-empty value (never blanks out existing data); explicitly does NOT touch job_id/stage/source/tags/recruiter_id (pipeline fields stay exactly as they were from the CSV import); logs an activity + audit entry. FRONTEND: AddCandidatePage.jsx's parsedToDraft() now carries the match info and a default _mergeChoice ('merge' for email match, 'create' for name-only match). Each draft review card shows an amber 'Matched existing candidate: X' banner with two radio options when a match exists (data-testid=draft-merge-radio-{i} / draft-create-radio-{i}); when 'merge' is selected, the Job/Source selects are hidden (since merge doesn't touch those fields) and a note explains what stays unchanged; the Save button becomes 'Merge into Existing Candidate' and calls the new merge-resume endpoint instead of POST /candidates, then navigates to the existing candidate's profile. NOT YET VERIFIED - needs backend testing first: (1) create a candidate via POST /candidates with a distinctive name and NO resume_file_id (simulating a CSV-imported candidate), then POST /api/resumes/parse with a resume fixture whose parsed name doesn't naturally match — actually to properly test, need to either edit a fixture's expected parsed name to match the seeded test candidate, or create a test candidate with name 'Sarah Chen' (matching the resume_sarah_chen.pdf fixture's actual parsed name) and email left blank, then parse that fixture and confirm the response's 'match' field shows match_type='name' and the correct candidate_id. (2) Also create a candidate with email 'sarah.chen@example.com' (matching that fixture's parsed email) and confirm match_type='email' is returned instead/with priority. (3) Call POST /api/candidates/{id}/merge-resume with the file_id + parsed data from step 1/2 and confirm the candidate's fields got updated (name/phone/title/company/location/skills/experience/education) while job_id/stage/tags/source/recruiter_id remained EXACTLY as before the merge, and resume_file_id now points to the new file. (4) Confirm a candidate with NO name/email match returns match=None and behaves exactly as the old create-new flow."

##         -comment: "USER REPORTED BUG: On the candidate profile page, resumes uploaded as .docx did not open/preview (unlike .pdf which worked fine). Root cause: the resume preview was a single <iframe src={blobUrl}> - browsers have a native built-in PDF renderer for iframes, but there is NO native browser renderer for Word/.docx documents, so the iframe showed blank/broken for docx files. Note: the app only accepts .pdf and .docx uploads (AddCandidatePage.jsx accept filter and resume_parser.py extract_text_from_bytes) - there is no legacy .doc (pre-2007 binary Word) support anywhere in the app, so 'the .doc format' in the user report refers to .docx. FIX: installed docx-preview (v0.4.0) npm package which parses OOXML .docx client-side into HTML. Restructured the resume-fetch effect in CandidateProfilePage.jsx to detect file type from response Content-Type header + Content-Disposition filename extension: if PDF -> keep existing iframe approach (unchanged); if DOCX -> store blob and render via docx-preview's renderAsync() into a dedicated container div (ignoreWidth/ignoreHeight so it reflows to fit the card); anything else -> graceful 'preview not available, use Download' message. Added loading/error states per type. Frontend restarted, webpack compiled successfully (only harmless docx-preview source-map warnings)."

##     -message: "NEW item to verify: resume auto-compression. User is planning to scale to ~50,000 candidates and was concerned about MongoDB storage (resumes stored as base64 blobs, 9.8GB volume). Implemented lossless PDF (PyMuPDF font-subset + garbage-collect + deflate) and DOCX (max-level re-zip) compression, auto-applied on every resume upload in routes_resumes.py's _store_file (used by both /api/resumes/parse and /api/resumes/parse/bulk), always falling back to the original bytes if compression fails or doesn't actually shrink the file. Text extraction for AI parsing runs on the ORIGINAL bytes before compression, so parsing accuracy is unaffected. Also retroactively compressed all 14 existing real resume files already in the database (2,084,531 -> 1,715,702 bytes, 17.7% avg reduction) and ran a Mongo compact to reclaim physical storage. Please test: POST /api/resumes/parse with /app/tests/fixtures/resume_sarah_chen.pdf and resume_priya_patel.docx — confirm 200, parsed fields look correct and complete (unaffected by compression), then GET /api/files/{file_id} for each and confirm the downloaded file is valid/openable and same size or smaller than the original. Also test /api/resumes/parse/bulk with 2-3 files. If frontend testing is later authorized, also spot-check that a freshly uploaded resume still previews correctly (PDF iframe / DOCX docx-preview) on the candidate profile page after being auto-compressed."

Please verify by: taking a candidate with a resume_file_id whose assigned job has description set but NOT jd_text, POST /api/candidates on that candidate (or trigger a background recompute by updating job_id), and after ~5s GET /api/candidates/{id} to confirm fit_score is now populated (0-100 integer) and fit_score_summary contains a non-empty explanation. ##     -agent: "main"
##     -message: "BUG FIX to verify (July 2026): user uploaded 4 resumes at once via the bulk parse UI, 2 succeeded and 2 failed with: `litellm.RateLimitError: OpenAIException - Error code: 429 - {'error': 'concurrent_request_limit', 'message': 'Unlock parallel requests by upgrading to Standard or Pro plan.', 'code': 'CONCURRENCY_REQUEST_LIMIT'}`. Root cause: routes_resumes.py's parse-bulk endpoint used `asyncio.gather` to fan out all _parse_one() calls in parallel — the Emergent LLM key's free-tier concurrent_request_limit rejected the excess. Fix: created backend/llm_helper.py with a module-level `LLM_SEMAPHORE = asyncio.Semaphore(1)` (configurable via LLM_CONCURRENCY env, default 1) and a `send_with_retry(chat, msg)` wrapper that awaits under the semaphore and retries on 429/CONCURRENCY_REQUEST_LIMIT/rate_limit errors with exponential backoff (2s, 4s, 8s, 16s, 32s + jitter, up to 5 tries). Wired the wrapper into both LLM call sites: resume_parser.py's parse_resume_text() (main + fallback JSON-repair call) and fit_scorer.py's _score_text(). This means even if the frontend chunks 10 files per parse-bulk request AND asyncio.gather fires all 10 in parallel, each LLM call queues on the semaphore and executes serially — no more 429s in practice.\n\nPlease test:\n1. POST /api/resumes/parse-bulk with 4 files at once (use /app/tests/fixtures/resume_sarah_chen.pdf, resume_priya_patel.docx, resume_miguel_torres.pdf, and one of them duplicated as a 4th file — this reproduces the exact user scenario of 4 concurrent resumes). Expect all 4 results to have status='success' with populated parsed fields. Time to complete may be ~20-40s total (serialized) — that's OK.\n2. POST /api/resumes/parse-bulk with 10 files (max chunk size the frontend sends). Same expectation: all 10 succeed, no 429s in response bodies or stderr.\n3. Verify existing single POST /api/resumes/parse still works — should be unaffected (single call, semaphore acquires immediately).\n4. Verify fit scoring path still works: pick a candidate with a resume whose job has description set, PUT /api/candidates/{id} touching job_id to retrigger recompute_candidate_fit background task, wait ~30s, GET the candidate and confirm fit_score is a fresh integer (not stale None).\n5. Check backend logs (/var/log/supervisor/backend.err.log) — should see zero `CONCURRENCY_REQUEST_LIMIT` or `429` errors AFTER the semaphore wrapper is in place. Any warning line like `LLM rate-limited (attempt X/5), backing off Ys` is EXPECTED and fine as long as the request eventually succeeds. Report the timing per file too so we can decide whether to raise LLM_CONCURRENCY later.\n\nDo NOT modify code — just test and report. Ignore the older bulk-limit-raise + fit-scorer-fallback changes, those were tested at the code level and are known working — focus solely on this concurrency fix."

##     -agent: "testing"
##     -message: "✅ LLM CONCURRENCY FIX FULLY VERIFIED - ALL 6 TESTS PASSED (100% success rate). Bug fix for user-reported issue (4 resumes uploaded, 2 failed with CONCURRENCY_REQUEST_LIMIT 429 error) is working correctly. Test results: (1) ✅ User scenario reproduction: Bulk parse with 4 files (resume_sarah_chen.pdf, resume_priya_patel.docx, resume_miguel_torres.pdf + duplicate) - ALL 4 parsed successfully in 8.3s with correct name/email extraction. ZERO 429 errors. (2) ✅ Stress test: Bulk parse with 10 files - ALL 10 parsed successfully in 21.1s (avg 2.1s per file). ZERO 429 errors. (3) ✅ Single parse regression: resume_sarah_chen.pdf parsed successfully, name='Sarah Chen' extracted correctly. (4) ✅ Fit score regression: Triggered recompute on candidate 'Olavo Guerra' for job 'VP/AVP of Delivery', waited 30s, fit_score=38 (valid int 0-100), fit_score_summary populated with coherent explanation. LLM retry logic working through semaphore. (5) ✅ Backend log check: ZERO 'CONCURRENCY_REQUEST_LIMIT' errors found in last 300 lines of backend.err.log. ZERO 'LLM rate-limited (attempt X/5)' retry warnings found - this indicates the semaphore is working perfectly by serializing LLM calls BEFORE they hit the concurrent request limit (no retries needed). (6) ✅ Sanity checks: GET /api/jobs (200), GET /api/candidates?limit=5 (200), GET /api/dashboard/stats (200) - no regressions. CRITICAL FINDINGS: The fix is working as designed - the LLM_SEMAPHORE (default=1) serializes all LLM calls across both resume parsing (resume_parser.py) and fit scoring (fit_scorer.py), preventing concurrent requests from ever reaching the Emergent LLM API's free-tier limit. The send_with_retry() wrapper with exponential backoff (5 attempts, 2s->32s) is in place as a safety net but wasn't needed in testing since the semaphore prevents 429s proactively. Performance: 4-file bulk parse completed in ~8s (acceptable for user scenario), 10-file stress test in ~21s (2.1s avg per file). Implementation is production-ready and solves the user's reported bug completely."

The backend constructs redirect_uri as {APP_BASE_URL}/api/oauth/calendar/callback, resulting in: https://ats-build-preview.preview.emergentagent.com/api/oauth/calendar/callback. Then restart backend service. OPTION 2: Add the EXACT redirect URI to Google Cloud Console as an Authorized Redirect URI: https://ats-build-preview.preview.emergentagent.com/api/oauth/calendar/callback. REQUIRED SCOPES (verify these APIs are enabled in Google Cloud Console): (1) https://www.googleapis.com/auth/calendar, (2) https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.send, (3) https://www.googleapis.com/auth/userinfo.email, (4) openid. CONCLUSION: This is NOT a code bug. The backend OAuth implementation is correct and production-ready. The issue is purely a configuration mismatch between backend/.env and frontend/.env that needs to be resolved by the user."

##     -message: "BUG-FIX / FEATURE: (1) Hide interview guest list from attendees, (2) Attach Job Description to Google Calendar invite. Changes are in /app/backend/google_calendar.py and /app/backend/routes_interviews.py.\n\nWhat changed in google_calendar.py: create_event() now sets guestsCanSeeOtherGuests=False, guestsCanInviteOthers=False, guestsCanModify=False, visibility='private' on the event body. update_event() re-asserts the same 4 privacy flags on every update (Google's Calendar API sometimes drops them when you PUT a full event), and now also accepts 'description' and 'summary' as updatable fields.\n\nWhat changed in routes_interviews.py: new helper _build_event_description(iv, cand, job) builds a rich event description containing: interview type, stage, role, candidate name + internal profile link, notes for interviewers, then a JOB DESCRIPTION section (job.jd_text or job.description, truncated at 6000 chars if longer) followed by a link to the public /careers/jobs/{slug} posting when a slug exists. _sync_calendar_on_create now fetches the job doc and uses this helper. _sync_calendar_on_update now also refreshes the description when notes/type/stage change (in addition to the previous start/end/attendees/location updates).\n\nTESTING (fresh /tmp/verify_interview_invite.py — do NOT touch backend_test.py). Admin: admin@ats.com / Admin@123. Backend URL from /app/frontend/.env + '/api'.\n\nContract-level tests we CAN run without actually creating a Google Calendar event (admin has no Gmail connected in the test env, so _sync_calendar_on_create no-ops gracefully — that's fine, we're not verifying the real Google event, just the code path and inputs):\n\n1) Unit test the _build_event_description helper directly: `from routes_interviews import _build_event_description` then call it with: (a) an interview dict {type:'panel', stage:'Onsite', notes:'Focus on system design'}, a candidate {id:'c1', name:'Jane Doe'}, and a job {title:'Senior Engineer', jd_text:'We are hiring for our platform team. You will design distributed systems.', slug:'senior-engineer'}. Assert the returned string contains ALL of: 'Interview type: Panel', 'Stage: Onsite', 'Role: Senior Engineer', 'Candidate: Jane Doe', '/candidates/c1', 'Focus on system design', 'JOB DESCRIPTION', 'We are hiring for our platform team', '/careers/jobs/senior-engineer'. (b) Same but job=None -> assert no 'JOB DESCRIPTION' in output but candidate name still present. (c) Same but job.jd_text is 8000 chars long -> assert the returned string is <= ~6300 chars and contains 'truncated'. (d) Interview with no notes -> assert 'Notes for interviewers' NOT present.\n\n2) Unit test the create_event / update_event body construction: monkeypatch google_calendar._service to return a MagicMock, then call create_event(fake_creds, ...) and inspect what body was passed to events().insert(). PUT with status='cancelled' → 200. ##     -agent: "main"
##     -message: "NEW FEATURE — Send emails to candidates (July 2025 session). Added POST /api/career/emails/send in backend/routes_career_security.py. Body: {candidate_ids:[...], template_key?, subject?, html_body?}. Uses existing send_template() when a template is picked with no overrides, otherwise uses a new email_templates.send_custom() helper for free-form or template-with-overrides emails (both go through the same Gmail credentials picker _pick_sender_creds → recruiter first, else any admin with connected Gmail). Each successful send: (a) logs to db.email_log, (b) inserts an audit_log 'career.email.sent' entry, (c) inserts an activities row (action='email_sent') so the send appears in the candidate's timeline. Guardrails: candidate_ids required non-empty, max 500; unknown template_key → 404; missing subject/body when no template → 422; candidates without email are gracefully counted as skipped_no_email; missing candidate IDs are skipped_missing. Response shape: {total, sent, failed, skipped_no_email, skipped_missing, results:[{candidate_id,name,email,sent,reason?,error?,gmail_id?,sender?}]}. Test env: no admin has connected Gmail here yet (verified during import step), so send attempts are expected to return reason='no_gmail_connected' with sent=false — the endpoint itself must not 500, must still classify skip reasons correctly, and must still be callable end-to-end. PLEASE TEST endpoint contract only (write /tmp/verify_send_email.py — do NOT touch backend_test.py). Admin login admin@ats.com / Admin@123 (see /app/memory/test_credentials.md). Backend URL from /app/frontend/.env + '/api'. Tests: (1) POST /api/career/emails/send with 1 candidate_id + template_key='application_shortlisted' → 200, total=1, response has 'sent'+'failed'+'skipped_no_email'+'skipped_missing'+'results'. (2) POST with 3 real candidate_ids + custom subject='Hello {{candidate_name}}' + html_body='<p>Hi {{candidate_first_name}}!</p>' → 200 total=3, results length 3 with each result having candidate_id/name/email/sent/reason fields. (3) POST with 1 candidate_id that has NO email field in DB → that result must have reason='no_email_on_candidate' and skipped_no_email=1. (4) POST with a fake candidate_id → that result has reason='candidate_not_found' and skipped_missing incremented; real ones still processed alongside. (5) POST template_key='does_not_exist_template' → 404. (6) POST with empty {candidate_ids:[]} → 422. (7) POST with no template_key AND no subject/html_body → 422. (8) POST with candidate_ids of 501 IDs → 422. (9) After a successful (or attempted-then-no_gmail) send, GET /api/candidates/{id}/timeline should include an 'email_sent' activity row for that candidate (verifies the activity log side-effect). NO frontend testing yet — I'll ask user separately."

##     -agent: "main"
##     -message: "PHASE 3 sensitive-field hiding + timeline fix (July 2025 session). Two small changes: (1) Fixed the email_sent timeline bug from prior testing — the activity insert in POST /api/career/emails/send was using wrong schema ({action, details}); now correctly calls log_activity(user, 'email_sent', message, candidate_id) which writes {type, message} matching the timeline endpoint's expectations. (2) Interview Panel visibility deep-dive on notes and scorecards: (a) GET /api/candidates/{id}/timeline now filters out other users' notes AND other users' internal activities (note / email_log / email_sent types) for interview_panel and legacy interviewer roles. Panelists see only their own notes and only their own internal activity trail. Vendors get the same filtering as they shouldn't see recruiter notes either. Access check on timeline was hardened: interview_panel gets 403 unless the candidate's job is in their team; vendor gets 403 unless they submitted this candidate. (b) POST /api/candidates/{id}/notes now enforces: legacy interviewer must be on an assigned interview; interview_panel must have the job in their team; vendor must be the submitter. (c) GET /api/interviews/{id}/scorecards — interview_panel/interviewer sees only their own scorecard until they submit theirs; after their own submission, they can see everyone's. (d) GET /api/candidates/{id}/scorecards — same rule per-interview: their own always visible; others' visible only for interviews where they've already submitted. Vendors get [] (no scorecard visibility at all). (e) Fixed submit_scorecard admin bypass to use is_admin_or_higher (was checking user['role'] == 'admin' which broke for super_admin post-migration). Fixed add_availability admin bypass same way. LIVE TEST PASSED: Admin adds private note to a candidate; interview_panel user on that job sees 0 notes in timeline; after panelist adds their own note, they see just their 1 note; admin sees both notes. Also verified internal activity types (note/email_log/email_sent) from admin are hidden from the panelist. NEEDS TESTING: (1) GET /api/candidates/{id}/timeline as interview_panel — only their own notes visible; other users' notes hidden; internal activities from other users hidden; other activity types (application, stage_change, interview_scheduled, feedback_submitted, resume_merged) still visible. (2) POST /api/candidates/{id}/notes as interview_panel — 200 if on team, 403 otherwise. (3) POST /api/candidates/{id}/notes as vendor — 200 only if they submitted; 403 otherwise. (4) GET /api/interviews/{id}/scorecards as interview_panel who hasn't submitted → only their own row (likely empty list); after they POST their scorecard → all interviewers' scorecards visible. (5) GET /api/candidates/{id}/scorecards as interview_panel → per-interview filtering. (6) GET /api/candidates/{id}/scorecards as vendor → []. (7) After sending an email via POST /api/career/emails/send, GET /api/candidates/{id}/timeline as admin includes an activity of type='email_sent' with a message containing the template/subject. THIS IS THE TIMELINE BUG FIX VERIFICATION."
